discovery: Development of static ultrahigh-pressure techniques (megabar to terapascal diamond anvil cells) opening matter at extreme compression to physical study

nominees.name: Ho-kwang (Dave) Mao
nominees.affiliation: Center for High Pressure Science and Technology Advanced Research (HPSTAR), Beijing, China

nominees.name: Leonid Dubrovinsky
nominees.affiliation: Bayerisches Geoinstitut, University of Bayreuth, Germany

motivation: Pressure is the cleanest thermodynamic variable for changing interatomic distances, and thereby electronic structure, without changing chemistry. Mao and Hemley turned the diamond anvil cell into a quantitative instrument: the ruby pressure scale, the first static megabar experiments, and in situ synchrotron X-ray and spectroscopic probes. Together these revealed metallisation, new phases of hydrogen and iron, and the hydride superconductors. Dubrovinsky's double-stage and toroidal anvils, combined with laser heating, extended controlled static compression to the terapascal regime. This made possible the synthesis and single-crystal structure solution of compounds previously thought impossible, along with direct tests of first-principles predictions such as electronic transitions in osmium and new polynitrides. Their work has made extreme compression a laboratory in which quantum theory of condensed matter is confirmed or refuted. It underpins planetary physics and the design of new functional materials.
